newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB to establish rural banking centres.
newsitem.headline: NAB to establish rural banking centres.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) said on Wednesday it would establish 66 rural business banking centres across Australia as part of a major boost to its rural and provincial services.

NAB said the centres would be established over the rest of 1997 and that mobile rural finance managers would be appointed progressively to each centre. This would lift the number of NAB's mobile rural managers to more than 150 from 35.
NAB said it already had 490 rural outlets and was Australia's largest rural bank with loans of A$5.7 billion to farmers.
The initiative is one of several recently announced by NAB including a new flexible fixed rate loan product specially for farmers.
NAB said it recognised its rural network as a strength and asset and today's move was designed to preserve that.

"Under the plans announced today, we will increase our support for rural Australia by putting more rural finance expertise into all regional and provincial areas," NAB Chief General Manager Frank Cicutto said in a statement.
NAB had given a high level of lending authority to its regional managers, Cicutto said. They would make on-the-spot decisions for 90 percent of lending proposals.
Ben Clark had been appointed to the new role of Rural and Provincial Agribusiness Development Adviser.
